effects: Pulls `assets` ftUSD (0x04E6…427B) from the signer into the vault, which deposits it into the yield wrapper.
Mints `assets` sftUSD vault shares (1:1) to `receiver`, which earns FT rewards per epoch from then on.
Settles and checkpoints the receiver's accrued FT rewards before minting, so nothing already earned is lost.
formats.shown: "Stake 9.020293 ftUSD" with the ftUSD amount and the receiver address; nothing names the sftUSD shares that are minted.

findings.title: deposit: the screen never says 1:1 sftUSD shares are minted to the receiver.
findings.evidence: EpochRewardsVault.sol _deposit: `_mint(to, shares)` with shares == assets (_convertToShares returns assets). Descriptor: intent "Stake ftUSD", field label "Receiver". Case 0: 9020293 sftUSD (0x137d…7234) 'in' to the signer. The reader said 'Unknown. The screen doesn't name a receipt token'.
findings.fix: Relabel the receiver field "sftUSD shares to", or make the intent "Stake ftUSD for sftUSD".

findings.title: deposit: the interpolatedIntent leaves out who gets the staked position.
findings.evidence: descriptor interpolatedIntent "Stake {assets}"; `receiver` is shown only as a field. deposit() mints shares to `receiver`, which can be any address.

cases.notes: The 9.020293 ftUSD out is shown exactly. The 9.020293 sftUSD in is implied by 'Stake' plus the receiver field, but the token is not named. The reader knew a staked position was created but not that it is a receipt token.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)
effects: Burns `assets` sftUSD shares (1:1) from `owner`. If the signer is not the owner, it spends the owner's sftUSD allowance to the signer.
Settles the owner's accrued FT rewards before the burn. Those rewards stay claimable.
The yield wrapper sends `assets` ftUSD to `receiver`, either now or through a withdrawal queue (queueId is non-zero when queued).
formats.shown: "Unstake 9.020293 ftUSD" with the amount, the receiver and the owner.

findings.title: withdraw: the interpolatedIntent omits the receiver and the owner.
findings.evidence: descriptor interpolatedIntent "Unstake {assets}"; withdraw() burns shares from `owner` and sends ftUSD to `receiver` through yieldWrapper.withdraw(assets, receiver).

findings.title: withdraw: ftUSD may be queued in the yield wrapper instead of paid now, and nothing says so.
findings.evidence: EpochRewardsVault.sol _withdrawWithQueueIds: `queueIdTo = yieldWrapper.withdraw(assets, receiver);` and withdrawWithQueueId doc: "return the yield wrapper queue ID (0 when immediate)". In case 1 the payout was immediate.
findings.fix: Add a note in the intent or label, e.g. "may be queued".

cases.notes: 9.020293 sftUSD burned (shown as unstaking 9.020293 ftUSD) and 9.020293 ftUSD received by the signer, who is the receiver. Both match.

effects: Settles the signer's accrued FT rewards from settled epochs.
Sends all claimable FT (0x2638…4ad9), capped at the vault's FT balance, to `to`. Any remainder stays accrued.
formats.shown: "Claim FT to <to>" with the recipient address; no amount.

findings.title: claim: the FT amount comes from storage and cannot be shown.
findings.evidence: EpochRewardsVault.sol _claim: `uint256 claimable = user.ftAccrued; ... paidGross = claimable <= bal ? claimable : bal; FT.safeTransfer(to, paidToUser);`. Case 2: 5418757227107670144465 FT 'in', with no amount on the screen.
findings.fix: None in calldata. Optionally say "all claimable FT" in the intent.

cases.notes: The FT arrival and the recipient are shown. The amount is not in calldata, so the reader knew the asset and the recipient but not the amount.

couldNotCheck: The yield wrapper (IftYieldWrapperV2, 0xb3422496006383d7fa83b3218670616e550747f9) is not in the directory. withdraw relies on its withdraw(assets, receiver) to deliver ftUSD to the receiver, and that call can queue the payout, so I could not check when and how the signer receives ftUSD. Case 1 shows an immediate payout.

deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver.worst: deposit: the screen never says 1:1 sftUSD shares are minted to the receiver.

withdraw(uint256 assets, address receive.worst: withdraw: the interpolatedIntent omits the receiver and the owner.
